cn-layers-models.title: Layers, Models & the URL Trace
cn-layers-models.intro: The canonical opener: narrate what happens when you type a URL with latency numbers at every hop — then defend any layer.
groups: Layered Models With Opinions

• OSI is a teaching taxonomy; TCP/IP 5-layer (physical/link/net/transport/app) is what engineers mean. Map protocols to layers instantly when asked.
• Encapsulation: app bytes → segment (TCP) / datagram (UDP) → packet (IP) → frame (Ethernet); each layer's header consumed by its peer on the far side.
• Why layers leak: NAT rewrites at net/transport boundary, TLS sits inside app but below HTTP semantics, QUIC merges transport+security — modern systems blur the textbook lines; saying so scores points.
• Cross-layer realities: MTU constrains everything above; PMTUD failures blackhole connections; middleboxes ossify protocols (why QUIC encrypts headers).
• Interview move: after reciting the stack, volunteer ONE interesting interaction between adjacent layers (e.g., MSS clamping vs VPN tunnels).
The Full URL Trace — Resolution

• Browser parses scheme/host/port; checks HSTS list first (http→https upgrade), then DNS caches: browser → OS stub → hosts file → recursive resolver.
• Recursive walk: root server (anycast, ~1500 instances) → TLD (.com) → authoritative NS; glue records in referrals break circularity. Cached per TTL incl. negative answers.
• DoH/DoT encrypts stub→resolver leg; ECS extension passes subnet hints for geo-sensitive answers (privacy tradeoff).
• Latency budget: cached ~0ms, cold recursion ~30-100ms — why resolvers prefetch popular names and serve-stale during outages (RFC 8767).
• Records you should define cold: A/AAAA, CNAME (not at apex!), ALIAS/ANAME vendor fixes, NS, MX, TXT, CAA, DS/DNSKEY.
The Full URL Trace — Transport

• Route to IP via BGP-chosen path, longest-prefix forwarding; anycast steers to nearest PoP for big CDNs/resolvers.
• ARP resolves next-hop MAC per LAN hop; NAT boxes rewrite addr:port pairs tracked in conntrack tables.
• TCP handshake SYN→SYN-ACK→ACK (~1 RTT); kernel completes before accept(); backlog queue sizing under load.
• TLS 1.3: keys in ClientHello → 1-RTT full handshake, 0-RTT resumption with replay caveats; ALPN negotiates h2/h3 inside the handshake.
• RTT floor physics: ~3.3µs/km in fiber; US coast-to-coast ~40ms minimum — use these numbers when justifying CDN edges and connection reuse.
The Full URL Trace — Application

• Request out: method/path/version, Host mandatory (1.1), headers, body. Response: status, caching headers, content.
• Server chain: LB terminates TLS → proxy/envoy routes → app middleware (auth/rate-limit) → handler → DB/cache hits (p50 few ms warm) → serialize back through the same gauntlet.
• Static assets divert to CDN edge: browser cache → service worker → edge (~20ms from user) → shield → origin; fingerprinted filenames + immutable = forever-cache.
• Render pipeline once HTML lands: DOM/CSSOM → render tree → layout → paint → composite; blocking scripts pause parser; long tasks >50ms hurt INP.
• End-to-end budget example to quote: DNS 0-30 + TCP 1RTT + TLS1.3 1RTT + req/server/resp 1-2RTT + render ~200-500ms → why h3 0-RTT + edge rendering exist.
Failure Signatures Per Layer

• DNS: NXDOMAIN (exists? typo? propagation?) vs timeout (resolver dead? UDP blocked?).
• L3/L4: RST = refused (listener down/firewall reject) vs silent timeout = dropped (filtered/down route).
• TLS: cert warnings (expired, wrong SNI, clock skew! — VM clocks lie), handshake stalls (MTU blackhole on ServerHello+cert big packets).
• HTTP: 5xx taxonomy — 502 upstream dead/crashed, 504 upstream slow, 503 deliberate overload shed; LB-generated vs app-generated distinction matters.
• App: 200-with-error-body anti-patterns, empty bodies, HTML error pages where JSON expected — client parsing explosions.
Drills & Follow-up Traps

• 'Page loads but images fail': asset-domain DNS, mixed-content blocking, CORS on fonts/images, CDN hotlink protection 403s.
• 'Works in curl, fails browser': proxies (env vars vs system), cookies/auth state, CORS preflight OPTIONS handling, compression/content-type differences.
• 'Slow only first time': cold caches everywhere (DNS, TLS no session reuse, JIT warmup, empty page cache) — enumerate warmup paths.
• 'Intermittent 1% failures': connection pool exhaustion, LB health-check flap, GC pauses crossing timeouts, retry storms amplifying — ask for percentiles not averages!
• Closing flex options: QUIC migration story (wifi→5G survives), post-quantum X25519MLKEM768 already default Chrome↔Cloudflare, ECH encrypting SNI — current-affairs signals.

cn-http-family.title: HTTP/1.1 → h2 → h3 & Web APIs
cn-http-family.intro: Protocol evolution, caching correctness, status-code hygiene, and API conventions that come up in every backend round.
groups: Version Evolution Story

• 1.0: connection-per-request. 1.1 (1997): keep-alive, chunked transfer, mandatory Host, pipeline (broken by HOL — never deployed widely).
• Workaround era: domain sharding (≤6 conns/host limit), sprite sheets, inlining — all symptoms of head-of-line blocking, obsolete under multiplexing.
• h2 (RFC 7540, 2015): binary framing layer, streams multiplexed over one TCP conn, HPACK header compression, flow control per stream; server push shipped dead (Chrome removed 2022).
• Residual problem: single TCP pipe still HOL-blocks on packet loss — one lost segment stalls ALL streams (measured throughput collapses at 2% loss).
• h3 (RFC 9000, 2022): QUIC streams recover loss independently, TLS 1.3 integrated, connection IDs survive IP changes, 0-RTT resumption; adoption ~30%+ of web requests via Chrome/CF/Meta by 2025.
Semantics: Methods, Status, Headers

• Idempotency matrix: GET/PUT/DELETE idempotent, POST not — fix retries with Idempotency-Key header stored against response (Stripe pattern) — THE answer to payment double-charge questions.
• Status hygiene: 400 validation vs 401 unauthenticated vs 403 unauthorized; 404 vs 410 gone; 409 conflict; 422 semantics; 429 + Retry-After; never 5xx for client mistakes.
• Header categories worth fluency: conditional (If-Match/If-None-Match), caching (Cache-Control/Vary), content negotiation (Accept*), forwarding (X-Forwarded-* trust boundaries!).
• Range requests power resume/streaming (206 partial content, If-Range consistency).
· CORS mechanics if asked: preflight OPTIONS, Access-Control-Allow-Origin/Headers/Methods, credentials mode — same-site vs cross-site cookie interplay.
Caching Correctness

• Freshness: Cache-Control max-age/s-maxage/no-cache(revalidate)/no-store(never)/immutable/private/public; Age accumulates across hops.
• Validation: ETag strong/weak(W/), If-None-Match→304 saves body only; Last-Modified coarser fallback.
• stale-while-revalidate serves instant + refreshes background; stale-if-error keeps serving during origin brownouts — resilience pattern interviewers love.
• Vary discipline: Vary: Accept-Encoding standard; Vary: User-Agent = cache explosion (avoid!); normalization rules at edge.
• Layered hit ratios: browser → SW → CDN edge → shield → origin; measure each (X-Cache/CF-Cache-Status); purge via surrogate keys/tag invalidation APIs — professional answer to the invalidation joke.
REST & API Design Conventions

• Nouns plural, verbs via methods; nesting ≤2 levels (?limit&cursor filters/pagination); cursor/keyset pagination over offset for stability under inserts.
• Error shape consistency: RFC 9457 problem+json (type/title/detail/instance) or house envelope — consistency beats cleverness.
• Versioning: URI pragmatic (/v2/), header purist; sunset windows communicated (Sunset header + deprecation docs).
• GraphQL tradeoff sound-bite: flexible clients pay complexity (N+1 resolution, caching harder, query cost limits needed).
• gRPC niche: internal east-west RPC with protobuf contracts, HTTP/2 streaming; external-facing usually REST/JSON still.
Compression & Payload Hygiene

• Bodies: gzip/brotli (brotli wins static/text); images avif/webp; don't recompress already-compressed formats.
• HPACK header table (h2); QPACK adaptive (h3); CRIME/BREACH lessons: never compress secrets alongside attacker-controlled input.
• Chunked vs content-length; trailers for checksums after body; early hints (103) let browsers preload while server thinks.
• Payload audits: gzip -9 vs brotli -11 deltas on real responses; header bloat (cookies!) often exceeds body cost on small APIs — trim domains.
• Security headers checklist: HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy — name-drop a few with purposes.
Interview Drills

• 'Why did we need HTTP/2?' — serial pipes, 6-conn caps, header redundancy; frame it as solving 1.1-era constraints.
• 'Why does h2 still feel slow on flaky networks?' — TCP HOL blocking; h3 fixes via stream independence; cite loss-throughput measurements.
• 'Design cache headers for a product page' — s-maxage 60 + SWR 300, private user widgets no-store, ETags for API JSON, purge on inventory change via tag.
• 'Idempotency end-to-end' — key generation client-side, server dedupe window, response replay on retry, TTL cleanup; mention exactly-once illusion honestly.
• 'What breaks when moving to h3?' — UDP-blocked networks fallback, MTU quirks on VPNs, LB support maturity, observability tooling gaps — balanced adoption answer.

cn-tcp-udp.title: TCP & UDP Mechanics
cn-tcp-udp.intro: Reliability machinery, congestion control, lifecycle states, and the packet-level trivia that separates memorizers from understanders.
groups: Reliable Byte Stream Internals

• Seq numbers count BYTES not segments; cumulative ACKs confirm prefix; SACK blocks report received-disjoint ranges → precise fast retransmit of actual holes.
• RTO from smoothed RTT ± 4×RTTVAR (Jacobson/Karels); min-RTO floors spurious retransmits; timestamps disambiguate wrapped seqs.
• Fast retransmit on 3 dupACKs; recovery: NewReno halves once/window; RACK uses time-based inference (modern default).
• Flow control: receiver advertises rwnd; sender limited by min(cwnd, rwnd); zero-window probes keep stalled flows alive.
• Delayed ACK (~40ms) × Nagle = classic small-write stall — chat/RPC set TCP_NODELAY; know this cold, it appears constantly.
Congestion Control Evolution

• Slow start doubles cwnd/RTT till ssthresh → AIMD adds ~1MSS/RTT; Reno halves on loss, CUBIC scales halving cubically with time-since-loss (Linux default).
• BBR: model-based — estimates BDP and RTprop, paces at optimal point instead of waiting for loss signals; huge gains on bufferbloat paths; fairness debates ongoing (v2 fixes).
• Bufferbloat: oversized dumbbell buffers add seconds of standing queue — CoDel/FQ-CoDel drop/mark oldest-sojourners to keep queues short.
• ECN marks instead of drops; DCTCP fine-grained in datacenters for tiny queues and low latency variance.
• Math flex: 10Gbps×100ms needs cwnd ≈ (10e9/8×0.1)/1460 ≈ 85k segments — why classic AIMD refills glacially after loss, motivating pacing/BBR.
Lifecycle States Forensics

• Open: SYN_SENT → ESTABLISHED; passive LISTEN → SYN_RCVD → ESTABLISHED (kernel completes before accept()).
• Close: FIN_WAIT_1/2 → TIME_WAIT (2×MSL ≈ 60s Linux) absorbing retransmitted FINs + stale duplicates; server-side close leaves TIME_WAIT on SERVER (design implication!).
• CLOSE_WAIT pileup = peer closed, YOUR code forgot close() — fd leak signature; find with ss -tan state close-wait | wc.
• TIME_WAIT storms on outbound = churn without pooling — real fix: connection pools/keepalive, tcp_tw_reuse(+timestamps) secondary.
• RST semantics: abortive close discards data, refused = no listener, stale-segment kill; SO_LINGER=0 trades FIN for RST.
Kernel Data Path & Offloads

• RX: NIC DMA → RSS hashes flows to queues → IRQs spread across cores → GRO aggregates segments before stack → socket buffer.
• TX: GSO/TSO batch segmentation to NIC; checksum offload defers to hardware; qdisc layers (fq/fq_codel) pace and shape.
• Socket buffer autotuning ranges (tcp_rmem/wmem) cap throughput = window/RTT if undersized; verify live with ss -tmi (cwnd, rtt, retrans visible!).
• Zero-copy paths: sendfile/splice file→socket; io_uring zc tx; AF_XDP/DPDK bypass kernels for NFV tier.
• Tuning lore: somaxconn backlog, tcp_max_syn_backlog, syncookies under flood, busy_poll for ultra-low-latency niches.
UDP, QUIC & When Connectionless Wins

• UDP = raw datagrams: apps own reliability/order/congestion — DNS, QUIC, games, VoIP, telemetry.
• Keep payloads <1472B (avoid fragmentation; PMTUD unreliable through middleboxes); application-level pacing mandatory (unlike TCP) — irresponsible UDP floods get throttled by operators.
• QUIC recap: streams independent loss recovery, crypto built-in, CID-based migration, userspace-deployable congestion control — transport evolution escaping kernel ossification.
• Head-of-line comparison to recite: h2-over-TCP loses segment → whole conn stalls; QUIC delivers untouched streams immediately (lossy-link win measured).
• Multicast/SCTP trivia tier: IGMP/PIM exist, SCTP multi-streaming telecom heritage — mention-and-move-on.
Packet-Level Debug Patterns

• tcpdump -i any -nn -w f.pcap port 443 + Wireshark decode (SSLKEYLOGFILE decrypts TLS); follow-stream view reads like a conversation.
• Signature patterns: 40ms sawtooth small writes = Nagle×delayed-ack; SYNs answered nothing = filtered; SYN-ACK ok then stall = MTU blackhole (clamp MSS!);
• zero-window announcements = app not reading; dupACK storms + retransmits = lossy path or policer; RST mid-session = idle-timeout NAT/firewall (keepalive shorter than gateway timeout).
• Counters that tell stories: nstat -az deltas (TcpRetransSegs, ListenDrops), ip -s link errors/drops, ethtool -S queue stats.
• Cloud-specific: security groups log drops silently (timeout-not-refuse), NAT gateway idle ~350-900s, jumbo-frame mismatch between subnets.

cn-dns-cdn.title: DNS & Content Delivery
cn-dns-cdn.intro: Global traffic steering: names resolving, content landing near users, and the failure war-stories interviewers collect.
groups: DNS Protocol & Record Zoo

• Message anatomy: header flags (RD/RA/AA), question, answer/authority/additional; labels ≤63B, names ≤255B; compression pointers.
• Records cold: A/AAAA, CNAME (never apex), ALIAS/ANAME vendor workarounds, MX priority, TXT (SPF/DKIM/domain verification), NS, SOA (serial/refresh/negative-TTL), SRV discovery, CAA CA-pinning, SSHFP/TLSA/DANE exotic.
• TTL strategy: stable infra days; failover endpoints 30-60s; pre-deploy lowering dance; negative caching bites during migrations.
• Zone internals: AXFR/IXFR transfers, split-horizon views (internal/external answers differ), dynamic updates niche.
• DNSSEC chain: KSK/ZSK signing, DS delegation trust anchor, validation failures SERVFAIL loudly — operational care required.
Recursive Resolution at Scale

• Resolver caches RRsets per TTL; prefetch popular names pre-expiry; serve-stale (RFC 8767) rides out authoritative outages — internet-scale resilience pattern.
• Anycast frontends + backend pools; response-rate limiting blunts reflection/amplification attacks (open-resolver hygiene).
• Privacy ladder: DoT (853), DoH (443 blends into web traffic), ODoH adds proxy anonymity splitting resolver knowledge.
• ECS passes /24 hints for geo-sensitive CDNs — privacy tradeoff, frequently disabled by default now.
• Failure drills: registrar hijack (registrar-lock + DNSSEC detection), lame delegations (NS pointing nowhere — monitor!), root outage riding on cached TTLs.
CDN Mechanics

• Pull model: miss → fetch from shield → origin; store per TTL; push/prewarm for launch spikes. Shield tier cuts cross-continent origin trips dramatically.
• Edge selection methods compared: DNS-GeoIP (coarse, cache-poisonable), anycast (natural proximity), RUM-telemetry steering (real-user RTTs drive mapping — modern best practice).
• What caches well vs not: static/media yes; personalized/dynamic pass-through or micro-cache seconds; API GETs selectively with auth-aware keys.
• Hit-ratio economics: 90%+ typical media; origin offload IS the cost story — egress $/GB dominates cloud bills; CDN arbitrage math impresses infra interviewers.
• Purge tooling: soft (mark stale) vs hard; tag/surrogate-key batch invalidation (Fastly/Cloudflare APIs) — the grown-up cache-invalidation answer.
Video Delivery Specifics

• ABR ladder: multiple renditions; player switches per bandwidth+buffer heuristics (dash.js/hls.js; native HLS Safari/iOS).
• Segments 2-6s; CMAF chunks (~0.5s) + LL-HLS partial segments/blocking reload cut glass-to-glass latency toward 2-5s.
• DRM trio Widevine/PlayReady/FairPlay via CPIX key exchange; signed playlist URLs expire; token-at-edge validates HMAC without origin hit.
• Netflix Open Connect architecture flex: two-tier CDN — server appliances INSIDE ISP networks filled off-peak (pre-positioning), custom hardware + ML placement; open-source OC hardware designs published.
• QoE metrics: startup <2s, rebuffer ratio <0.5%, avg bitrate delivered; player beacons feed per-title encoding optimization loops.
Edge Compute & Security Layers

• Workers/Lambda@Edge run JS/WASM ms-from-users: auth rewrites, A/B assignment, bot scoring, personalization at edge with KV replicas.
• DDoS layering: volumetric absorbed by anycast spread/scrubbing centers; L7 challenges (JS proofs/captchas); rate limits per IP/JA3/session; WAF managed rulesets (OWASP core).
• Bot management: fingerprint heuristics + ML classification; TLS-fingerprinting catches scripted clients; honeypot endpoints feed blocklists.
• Multi-CDN strategy: RUM-driven steering across providers, health-checked failover, per-provider cost curves — real infra-interview flex material.
• Signed URLs/cookies for private assets; short-TTL tokens bound replay windows; audit logs at edge for compliance.
War Stories & Probes

• 'Site down, origin healthy' → DNS misconfig/registrar expiry, bad CDN config push, edge cert expiry, firewall blocking CDN IP ranges (allowlists stale).
• 'One country slow' → PoP gap, transit congestion visible in RUM maps, GeoDNS pointing far, peering dispute — triangulate with vantage points.
• 'Stale content after deploy' → missing versioned filenames or missed purge; immutable+hashed names kill the class entirely.
• 'DNS suddenly 5s' → dead NS in rotation timing-out before next tried, AAAA present but unroutable (happy-eyeballs should mask... check v6 path), resolver overload.
• Monitoring pitch: synthetic probes from regions, RUM percentiles per geography, DNS success-rate per resolver, cert expiry ladders (60/30/7d alerts).

cn-routing-switching.title: Routing, Switching & the Internet Fabric
cn-routing-switching.intro: Below sockets: MACs, VLANs, BGP politics, anycast economics — infrastructure-flavored rounds dig here.
groups: L2 Switching Fundamentals

• Switches learn MAC→port mappings from source addresses; unknown/unicast flooded; broadcast always flooded within VLAN.
• Frames carry MAC src/dst + VLAN tag (802.1Q 4-byte insert); trunk ports carry tagged, access ports untagged.
• Loops killed by spanning tree (STP/RSTP) — blocked redundant links until topology change; convergence seconds matter in incidents.
• MTU end-to-end: 1500 classic, jumbo 9000 datacenter-internal (storage/replication love it); mismatch = fragmentation or blackhole depending on DF bit.
• ARP: broadcast question who-has-IP → MAC reply, cached; gratuitous ARP announces moves; ARP spoofing → dynamic ARP inspection defenses.
L3 Forwarding & Protocols

• Longest-prefix match against FIB; control plane (routing protocols) feeds it; hardware tables do line-rate lookup.
• ICMP: echo, unreachable, TTL-exceeded (traceroute mechanism), frag-needed (PMTUD!) — filtering frag-needed breaks connections mysteriously (VPN classic).
• DHCP: discover-offer-request-ack; option 82 relay info; reservations for infra.
• IPv6 coexistence: dual-stack preferred over tunnels; SLAAC vs DHCPv6; the 'it works except v6 path broken' class of bugs (happy eyeballs masks until it doesn't).
• NAT flavors: SNAT/masquerade outbound, DNAT port-forwards inbound, full-cone/restricted variants affect P2P hole punching.
Interior Gateway Protocols

• OSPF: link-state, Dijkstra SPF per area, flooding LSAs; areas contain scope; DR/BDR elections on broadcast nets.
• IS-IS: CLNP heritage, carrier-grade cousin — same link-state ideas, runs directly over L2.
• Metrics: cost ∝ inverse-bandwidth typically; ECMP spreads across equal costs (hash per-flow preserving ordering).
• Convergence events: neighbor death timers vs BFD millisecond detection — sub-second failover requires BFD pairing.
• Datacenter fabrics: spine-leaf topologies, equal-cost everywhere, VXLAN overlays abstract tenants above the fabric — modern cloud network mental model.
BGP — The Internet's Glue

• Path-vector protocol between ASes; policies (business relationships) outrank pure metrics — cold potato vs hot potato routing shapes user experience.
• Attributes: AS_PATH, LOCAL_PREF (outbound preference), MED (hints to neighbors), communities (policy tags).
• Route reflection/confederations scale iBGP meshes; RPKI/ROA signing fights route hijacks (YouTube-Pakistan 2008 cautionary tale).
• Anycast economics: same prefix announced globally from many sites; BGP naturally pulls users to nearest announcement — DNS roots, CDNs, public resolvers.
• Incident literacy: BGP leaks (Facebook 2021 self-inflicted withdrawal), hijacks, route leaks — reading bgp.tools/RISlive during interviews shows practitioner flavor.
Load Balancing & Traffic Engineering

• ECMP hashing: 5-tuple hash keeps flow affinity; consistent-hash variants survive pool membership changes better (maglev/supersetting papers).
• L4 vs L7 balancing: DSR modes bypass return-path LB; L7 sees URLs/headers enabling routing/stickiness/compression.
• GSLB: DNS-based geographic steering weighted by health/load — coarse but global; pair with per-region anycast for precision.
• Telemetry: flow sampling (NetFlow/IPFIX/sFlow), per-hop latencies, loss maps drive engineering decisions.
• Capacity planning: 95th-percentile billing models shape burst strategies; transit vs peering mix decisions (open peering policy culture wars).
Hands-On Fluency Checklist

• iproute2: ip addr/link/route/neigh, ss -tlnp; bridge/vlan ops; tc for shaping experiments.
• Read a traceroute: asterisk semantics (ICMP-filtered ≠ dead), MPLS labels leaking, asymmetric return paths lying to you.
• Wireshark L2-L3 hunts: ARP storms, STP topology-change bursts, PMTU failures, ECMP reordering artifacts.
• Lab muscle: containerlab/GNS3/vagrant virtual labs — being able to SAY you've broken fixed BGP sessions lands differently than theory alone.
• Cloud translation: VPCs are overlay fabrics, route tables + security groups replace routers/ACLs, TGW/VPC-peering topologies mirror classic hub-spoke — translate freely both directions.

cn-security-tls.title: TLS, PKI & Wire Security
cn-security-tls.intro: Handshake mechanics, certificate ecosystems, attack classes, and the post-quantum transition happening right now.
groups: TLS Handshake Internals

• TLS 1.2: ClientHello → ServerHello+Cert+ServerKeyExchange(ECDHE sig) → client key exchange → Finished ×2 — 2 RTT before app data.
• TLS 1.3: key_share sent eagerly in ClientHello; server responds complete in ONE RTT; 0-RTT early-data on resumption — replay risk means idempotent-only payloads (GETs, deduped POSTs).
• Key schedule: HKDF chains from shared secret (ECDHE X25519 dominant); transcript hash binds everything — tamper anywhere breaks Finished.
• Cipher suites collapsed: AEAD-only (AES-GCM/ChaCha20-Poly1305); ChaCha preferred without AES hardware (mobile!); forward secrecy universal now.
• Session resumption: tickets (stateless-ish, encrypted state) or PSK; ticket rotation + key hygiene matter (ticket key compromise decrypts captures!).
PKI & Certificate Operations

• Chain validation: leaf → intermediates → trusted root; name matching SANs (CN deprecated); validity window, key usage extensions enforced.
• Revocation reality: CRLs heavy, OCSP slow/privacy-leaky → OCSP stapling (server embeds fresh proof) + short-lived certs trend; CRLite coming.
• Let's Encrypt economy: ACME automation, 90-day lifetimes normalizing; cert-manager in k8s; internal mTLS mesh (SPIFFE identities) mirrors the model internally.
• SNI lets one IP host many certs; ECH (Encrypted Client Hello) rolling out hides hostnames from observers — privacy milestone worth citing.
• Pinning history lesson: HPKP died (bricking risk); today: CT logs (certificate transparency — public ledger, monitor for rogue issuance) + Expect-CT legacy.
Attack Classes & Mitigations

• Downgrade/strip attacks: HSTS preloaded forces https; ALPN inside handshake prevents protocol downgrade; fallback logic removed from modern stacks.
• Historical cipher/archaeology: BEAST (CBC IV), POODLE (SSLv3 padding), RC4 biases, Logjam (export DH), FREAK — why config scanners still matter (testssl.sh).
• Implementation bugs: Heartbleed (heartbeat overread), ROBOT (RSA padding oracle) — patch cadence + fuzzing culture answer.
• Traffic analysis beyond encryption: SNI (ECH fixing), sizes/timing (padding + batching partial), DNS visibility (DoH helps).
• MITM positions: corporate TLS-inspection appliances break pinning assumptions + PQ handshakes — enterprise friction stories show real-world depth.
Application-Layer Wire Security

• Cookie armor: Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax/Strict, __Host- prefix; session fixation defenses (rotate on login).
• CSRF vs CORS confusion untangler: CSRF = browser auto-sends creds cross-site; CORS governs READ access — orthogonal; SameSite largely kills classic CSRF.
• JWT-on-the-wire choices: authorization bearer vs DPoP/mTLS sender-constraining; alg:none horror stories → allowlist algorithms explicitly.
• API keys vs OAuth tokens vs mTLS — threat-model each: replayability, revocation, audience binding.
• Rate limiting + bot tiers at edge (from CDN section) tie-in: JA3/JA4 fingerprints catch scripted abuse cheaply.
Post-Quantum Transition (Now)

• Shor's algorithm threatens RSA/ECDH eventually; harvest-now-decrypt-later makes long-secret traffic urgent TODAY.
• Hybrid X25519MLKEM768 (ML-KEM = Kyber standardized as FIPS 203) default in Chrome + Cloudflare since 2024 — largest PQ deployment ever; quote it as current affairs.
• Signatures lag (bigger sizes); ML-DSA (Dilithium) standardization trailing KEMs; cert bloat concerns for constrained devices.
• Performance reality: hybrid handshakes add ~KB overhead, negligible RTT impact — measured, not feared.
• Talking points: inventory crypto dependencies, plan agility (swap curves without redesign), watch NIST timelines — pragmatic PQ readiness narrative.
Ops Fluency Checklist

• openssl s_client -connect host:443 -servername host -alpn h2 — read chain, verify dates/protocols by hand.
• testssl.sh / SSL Labs grading; internal CA hierarchies (root offline, intermediate issuing, CRL/OCSP responders HA).
• mTLS rollout pains: cert rotation automation, SNI-vs-verification mismatches, proxy passthrough vs termination decisions.
• Secrets on the wire beyond TLS: SSH hardening (cert-based CAs, no passwords), wireguard for site-links, Vault Transit for crypto-as-service.
• Monitoring: handshake failure-rate spikes (client-version cliffs), stapling staleness, CT-log monitoring alerts for your domains.

cn-web-realtime.title: Realtime Web: SSE, WebSockets & WebRTC
cn-web-realtime.intro: Push technologies compared honestly, fan-out architectures, presence systems, and delivery-semantics traps.
groups: Push Technology Decision Tree

• Polling: dumb-simple, wasteful at scale — baseline to beat. Long-poll: hold request till event/timeout, reconnect loop — works through anything, awkward scaling.
• SSE: server→client unidirectional over plain HTTP; EventSource API auto-reconnects w/ Last-Event-ID; text/event-stream framing — perfect for feeds/notifications/LLM streaming tokens (ChatGPT-style UIs use it!).
• WebSocket: full-duplex single TCP after upgrade handshake (h1.1 Upgrade headers); binary frames, subprotocols; needs LB idle-timeout awareness + sticky sessions OR shared pub/sub behind stateless gateways.
• WebTransport (h3): streams + unreliable datagrams, multiplexed without HOL — the future for games/quizzes; WebRTC data channels for P2P today.
• Selection heuristic: one-way updates → SSE (simplest ops); bidirectional interactive → WS; P2P media/data → WebRTC; lossy-fast → WebTransport datagrams.
WebSocket Infrastructure Realities

• LB config: idle timeouts > heartbeat interval; sticky sessions unnecessary IF state lives in Redis/pub-sub keyed by connection registry.
• Heartbeats: ping/pong frames detect half-open connections (NAT silently drops) — 30s cadence typical; missed pongs trigger teardown + reconnect with jittered backoff.
• Backpressure: per-connection send queues with bounds; slow consumers evicted or downsampled (feed pagination hints) — unbounded queues OOM nodes.
• Scale numbers: single node 100k-1M concurrent sockets depending on language/frame size; connection churn during deploys causes thundering reconnects — drain gracefully, jitter client retries exponentially.
• Auth: ticket flow (short-lived WS ticket from HTTPS API) avoids sending JWT in URL/query logs; re-auth on reconnect; per-message authorization for sensitive channels.
Fan-Out & Delivery Semantics

• Publish path: event → Kafka/topic → per-node subscribers via Redis pub/sub or direct registry; sharded channel routing for celebrity-scale rooms.
• Delivery guarantees menu: at-most-once (drop on disconnect), at-least-once (client cursors + redelivery), exactly-once illusion (dedupe ids client-side) — pick per feature, say WHY.
• Ordering: per-channel sequence numbers; gap detection triggers snapshot refill (missed-events endpoint) rather than buffering forever.
• Presence: heartbeated membership sets (Redis ZSET scored by last-beat); online/idle/away transitions; fan presence deltas only to interested parties (friends lists) — naive presence broadcasts murder infra.
• Typing indicators/read receipts: fire-and-forget ephemeral (at-most-once fine) — distinguishing durability classes per message type is the senior answer.
WebRTC Deep Cut

• Signaling: SDP offer/answer exchanged via YOUR channel (WebSocket); ICE gathers candidates (host/srflx/relay) — trickle ICE streams them.
• NAT traversal: STUN discovers reflexive address; TURN relays when symmetric NAT blocks (~10-20% of connections need TURN — budget bandwidth $$!).
• DTLS-SRTP encrypts media; ICE consent freshness checks; connection state machine handling (failed → ICE restart).
• SFU topology scales group calls (Selective Forwarding Unit forwards simulcast layers); mesh dies past ~4 participants; MCU legacy transcodes.
• Use cases beyond video: data channels for game state (unordered/unreliable mode!), file transfer, collaboration cursors — flexibility talking point.
Notification Pipelines

• Architecture: producer services → notification bus → orchestrator (dedupe, preferences, quiet hours) → channel adapters (push APNs/FCM, email SES, SMS, in-app SSE).
• Fan-out on write vs read for in-app feeds ties back to feed case studies; notifications usually hybrid (celebs aggregated, normals pushed).
• Idempotency keys prevent duplicate pushes across retries; provider receipts reconcile delivery states.
• Batching/digest policies reduce alert fatigue (product metric!); unsubscribe compliance (email legalities) surface in design reviews.
• Observability: delivery funnel metrics (queued→sent→delivered→opened), per-provider latency/error dashboards, poison-pill quarantine queues.
Interview Drill Bank

• 'Design live comments' → SSE + Redis pub/sub + shard-by-video-id, cursor refill on reconnect, presence optional.
• 'Collaborative doc cursors' → WS + CRDT library (Yjs/Automerge) server-relayed, presence via ephemeral channels — name CRDT vs OT tradeoffs briefly.
• 'Live sports scores at superbowl scale' → write-time fan-out prohibitive → read-time merge + edge micro-caching (1-2s TTL) + SSE long-lived conns; jittered refresh.
• 'Chat delivery guarantees' walkthrough → per-conversation seq, ack windows, offline queue with TTL, dedupe ids, read markers sync.
• 'Why not just poll?' honest answer sometimes: simplicity wins at small scale; realtime justified by UX need + cost curve — judgment signal beats tech-maximalism.

cn-tools-debugging.title: Network Debugging Toolkit
cn-tools-debugging.intro: The hands-on round: commands, signatures, and triage trees that prove you've actually debugged packets.
groups: Core Toolbox Cheat Sheet

• curl flags: -v verbose, --resolve host:port:ip (bypass DNS), -H headers, --limit-rate (slow-client simulation), -o /dev/null -w '%{time_connect} %{time_starttransfer}' timing breakdown.
• dig +short / @resolver / +trace (walk hierarchy); drill specific record classes quickly.
• tcpdump -i any -nn -s0 -w f.pcap 'tcp port 443'; read later in Wireshark; -A/-X quick ASCII peeks; capture filters (BPF) beat display filters for volume.
• ss -tanp / -tlnp / state filters; -i shows cwnd/rtt/retrans per socket — live TCP vitals.
• nstat -az counter deltas (TcpExt* goldmine); ip -s link error counters; ethtool -S queue-level stats.
Latency Decomposition Method

• curl timing vars tell WHERE time goes: dns → connect (TCP) → appconnect (TLS) → starttransfer (server think) → total.
• Pattern: connect high + rest fine = network path/RTT issue; appconnect high = TLS/CPU/cert-chain issue; starttransfer high = server/backend slowness.
• Compare same-origin from multiple vantage points (laptop, bastion in-region, synthetic probe) — localize fault domain fast.
• Percentiles over means ALWAYS; capture histograms (curl in loop + awk bucketing quickie).
• Correlate with server-side: LB target response times vs client-observed — difference = network/queueing outside app.
Packet Signature Field Guide

• SYN→SYN-ACK delta = clean RTT sample; SYN unanswered = drop/filter; SYN then RST = port closed/refused.
• DupACKs + fast retransmits = loss; spurious retransmits (RACK flags) = aggressive timers/NAT timeouts.
• Zero-window + window probes = receiver app stalled (backpressure found!); MTU blackhole: handshake OK, large packets stall, ICMP frag-needed absent (PMTUD broken).
• 40ms sawtooth on small writes = Nagle×delayed-ack (fix TCP_NODELAY); RST after idle period = NAT/firewall idle-timeout (add keepalive < timeout).
• TLS: ClientHello w/o ServerHello = SNI-based blocking or cert issues; alert frames decode reasons (handshake_failure, certificate_expired).
TLS & Cert Triage Tree

• openssl s_client -connect h:443 -servername h: verify chain manually; -brief for quick protocol/cipher confirmation.
• Symptom: works curl, fails Go/Java → incomplete chain (server sends leaf only; curl carries AIA fetching, strict clients don't) — fix chain order on server.
• Clock skew on VMs breaks validation ('certificate not yet valid') — chrony health first, certificates second.
• SNI mismatches when IPs shared across tenants; ECH rollout surprises on old middleboxes; ALPN negotiation failures breaking h2-only servers.
• Expiry ops: cert-manager renewal loops, ACME rate-limit stomps (staging endpoint for tests!), deploy-day cert bundles pinned in images going stale.
DNS Debug Playbook

• Isolate level: local cache (flush), resolver (@1.1.1.1 vs default), authority (query NS directly with dig +norecurse).
• +trace shows delegation walk; compare TTLs across resolvers mid-migration; check BOTH A and AAAA (broken v6 = intermittent hangs).
• Propagation myths: TTL-driven caching, negative caching bites during rollbacks; registrar glue records must match new NS hostnames (in-zone dependencies!).
• Split-horizon confusion: internal resolver returns private answers — test from correct network context; VPN DNS leakage stories.
• DNSSEC failures SERVFAIL with clues: dig +dnssec, validate chain manually, watch for rollover mishaps (KSK stuck in old state).
Structured Triage Narratives

• Tell it as tree, not stream: 'Scope (who/where/how many) → Localize (layer via signatures above) → Hypothesize (rank by base rate) → Test cheapest-first → Fix + guardrail.'
• Guardrails vocabulary: synthetic probes catching regressions, dashboards per dependency, runbooks linking alarms → playbooks, postmortems feeding lint/tests.
• War-story template practiced per layer: DNS story, TCP story, TLS story, app story — 90-second versions ready.
• Tooling maturity flex: eBPF-based continuous network observability (pixie/cilium hubble), flow logs pipelines, chaos experiments injecting latency/loss validating client behavior (toxiproxy/tc netem).
• Close interviews asking THEIR debugging stack — turns interrogation into peer conversation, memorable finish.
